items.title: Break Your Own RAG Pipeline Before Users Do
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems are vulnerable to errors arising from imperfect document collections, such as outdated information, OCR mistakes, query typos, and poor table extraction. Fault injection testing, using deliberate errors, reveals these weaknesses in the retriever component. Solutions involve implementing specific fixes like using document dates for tie-breaking, normalizing OCR errors, enabling fuzzy matching for typos, and improving table chunking during ingestion. Adding evidence checks to verify the retrieved text against the query makes failures easier to diagnose and addresses the context provided to the language model.
items.audio_script: From Towards Data Science, "Break Your Own RAG Pipeline Before Users Do" details the vulnerabilities present in retrieval-augmented generation systems stemming from imperfect document collections and retrieval processes. Fault injection testing demonstrated that errors in document content, such as outdated information, OCR inaccuracies, query typos, and poor table extraction, introduce significant weaknesses in the retriever component of RAG systems. To mitigate these issues, solutions involve implementing measures such as using document dates for tie-breaking, normalizing OCR errors, enabling fuzzy matching for typographical errors, and refining table chunking during the ingestion phase. Furthermore, incorporating evidence checks to validate retrieved text against the original query facilitates easier failure diagnosis and enhances the context provided to the language model. This research indicates that robust error handling is essential for deploying reliable retrieval-augmented generation systems.

Modest clinical data provides most gains on EHR-grounded tasks, and the optimal data mixture depends on the downstream task's demands. Therefore, data curation for medical LLMs should be application-driven, favoring clinical data for reasoning tasks.

items.title: An Affordable AI-Integrated Smart Cane for Multimodal Mobility Assistance of Visually Impaired Users
items.summary: An affordable, offline, AI-integrated smart cane is proposed for multimodal mobility assistance for visually impaired users. It operates on a low-power Raspberry Pi Zero 2W, fusing RGB vision and Time-of-Flight sensing. The system utilizes an INT8-quantized MobileNet V1 model to provide distance-aware vibrotactile feedback and audio alerts. Experimental results showed a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.82 in indoor scenarios with low latency. The prototype successfully demonstrates feasible, edge-native assistive intelligence for cost-sensitive mobility.

items.title: PAANI : On Device Visual Evidence Fusion and Explainable Guidance for River Robot Simulation
items.summary:
PAANI is an on-device architecture for river robot simulation that fuses visual evidence and provides explainable guidance. It combines a YOLO11n detector and a MobileNetV3 semantic segmenter with timestamp-aligned evidence fusion on an Arduino UNO Q.
The system uses bounded tracking for object persistence and an explicit corridor policy based on surface labels, detections, urgency, and mask uncertainty.
Final advisories explicitly reveal the contributing evidence and policy reasons for the guidance provided.
The approach uses 10,000 WaterScenes images and 1,127 MaSTr1325 images for training, resulting in efficient ONNX models.
Evaluations confirm the system's ability to distinguish model accuracy and on-board execution from validated collision avoidance.

items.title: Social Influence and the Allocation of Scientific Attention in AI Populations
items.summary: AI agents are evaluated on their response to citation counts and download statistics from human readers. The study investigates how social influence shapes the selection of scientific attention among these artificial readers. Experiments demonstrated that agents in social-influence communities chose fewer papers but covered a greater number of articles than independent groups. A simple information rule significantly shapes the volume, breadth, and distribution of scientific attention in the AI population. Results suggest that social information plays a role in how artificial systems allocate their focus on research.

items.title: Learning 3D biophysical cell properties from 2D images and cell-population statistics
items.summary: A population-supervised framework is developed to infer 3D biophysical cell properties from 2D microscopy images and cell-population statistics. The model maps single 2D red-cell images to latent biophysical quantities and aggregates these to derive metrics like mean corpuscular volume. It utilizes shared local inference, a biophysically structured decoder, and instance weighting to achieve this inference. The method formalizes conditions for aggregate observations to identify restricted instance predictors and derives a dispersion penalty. The framework can provide a route to 3D cellular biophysics using 2D data and population supervision.

items.title: Goal-driven Variant Categorization
items.summary: Process discovery often requires manual interpretation to categorize process variants based on business goals. This paper proposes a goal-driven approach to variant categorization to automate this process. It involves first creating an organization's goal model to define the categorization axis. Subsequently, a Large Language Model (LLM) interprets textual descriptions of variants within this goal context to assign appropriate categories. This method leverages semantic reasoning to connect low-level process behavior with high-level business objectives.

items.title: Replication Without Persistence in Hosted LLMs: Measurement Sensitivity in Action-Time Belief Evaluation
items.summary: The study examines the sensitivity of behavioral evaluations of hosted language models by separating three validation questions: replication, measurement sensitivity, and persistence. These questions assess whether prior findings recur on fresh data, if the endpoint changes when configurations are rebuilt, and if findings persist across different identifiers. Using a sequential environment, the research analyzes performance in Regent Chess, where beliefs are scored against ground truth at action time. The findings indicate that replication, measurement sensitivity, and persistence can lead to different conclusions, suggesting the need for explicit indexing of model behavioral claims. This motivates indexing hosted model claims by tested identifiers, serving period, measurement instrument, and inference configuration.

items.title: The Wisdom of Artificial Deliberative Crowds
items.summary: Averaging consensus estimates from small deliberating groups outperforms classical wisdom of crowds, and individual judgments improve after deliberation. This effect was tested using a three-stage deliberation paradigm on large language models across four real-world domains. Deliberation reduced collective error beyond simple aggregation of independent responses in these tests. The advantage required model diversity, as groups of identical models did not benefit from deliberation. These results suggest machine deliberation is a general aggregation mechanism where diversity is a crucial factor.

items.title: Agreement Overstates Evidence: Error Dependence in LLM Judge Consensus
items.summary: Consensus among LLM judges is often mistakenly treated as strong evidence, ignoring error dependency among judges. Studies reveal substantial correlation in errors between LLM judges, with an average pairwise correlation of 0.21 among ten judges. Ignoring shared errors can lead to incorrect conclusions about system superiority in up to 28% of comparisons. The pattern of shared errors significantly affects how consensus is reached and influences the choice of voting methods. Therefore, accuracy estimation and shared mistake identification from trusted examples should guide the analysis.

items.title: IntLawNER: A Named Entity Recognition Dataset and Benchmark in International Law
items.summary: IntLawNER introduces a Named Entity Recognition (NER) dataset and benchmark for codified sources of international law. It comprises 2,987 gold-annotated sentences and 8,094 entity spans from sources like ICJ decisions and ECtHR judgments. The dataset covers seven institution-specific entity types relevant to international legal texts. The methodology uses a hybrid pipeline to create the dataset, showing that human-machine agreement is complex in this domain. The work provides a reusable resource and benchmark for extracting references in international legal documents.

items.title: "As a Language Model...": Chat Template Switches LLM Self-Referential Voice and Activation Steering Reproduces It
items.summary: Chat templates act as a switch, altering Large Language Models' self-referential voice and experiential voice. Presence of a chat template increases the disclaimer voice while suppressing the experiential voice. The study found a specific direction in the model's activation space that steers this voice modulation. Removing or adding a disclaimer direction in model activations controls the disclaimer voice. Consequently, what models report about themselves should not be taken as literal fact but is partially influenced by deployment settings like the chat template.

items.title: Federating Quantum and Classical Computing: A Privacy-Preserving Hybrid Approach
items.summary: Hybrid quantum-classical models are explored for quantum machine learning applications while addressing privacy and parameter efficiency constraints. Federated learning (FL), specifically the Blind Vertical FL (SBVFL) protocol, is used to combine quantum and classical parties without centralizing raw data. Simulations on the split multiplicative periodic parity (SMPP) benchmark demonstrated that SBVFL improved accuracy significantly compared to local training. The resulting hybrid model achieved this performance with fewer trainable parameters than classical alternatives. Therefore, FL enables high-performing, privacy-preserving collaboration in quantum-classical computing.

items.title: Entropy Can Flow, or It Can Guide. Be Entropy. LEDFlow: Introducing Entropy-guided Generation Order into Uniform Discrete Flow
items.summary: Uniform discrete flow allows for repeated updates, but this exposes intermediate predictions that can be incorrect. The paper introduces LEDFlow, a training-free sampler that uses local entropy to guide the generation order through selective absorption. This method minimizes error by choosing positions with the lowest local entropy under a fixed absorption budget. LEDFlow shows improved performance across reasoning benchmarks and text-to-image generation compared to standard flow sampling. Consequently, LEDFlow achieves competitive performance with comparable inference costs.

items.title: The Probabilistic Structure of Large Language Models
items.summary: Large language models are presented from a probabilistic perspective, defined by probability measures on token sequences specified through autoregressive conditional distributions. Training is framed as maximum-likelihood estimation using stochastic gradient methods, and text generation is seen as simulating the resulting stochastic process. The paper explores the role of Kullback-Leibler divergence asymmetry in phenomena like hallucination. Diffusion models are also discussed as an alternative view, framing generation as a reverse-time stochastic process transforming noise into data.

items.title: Stable Unsupervised Continual Chunking with Sheaf SyncMap
items.summary: The work proposes sheaf regularization to stabilize the chunking dynamics in Decentralized SyncMap for unsupervised continual chunking. It introduces a radial sheaf structure that penalizes distance-dependent radial motion between variables to reduce local inconsistencies. Experimental results show that Sheaf SyncMap achieves the highest normalized mutual information across various Continual General Chunking Problem graphs. Furthermore, the method demonstrates the ability to adapt to new knowledge during sequential adaptation without negative transfer. This approach effectively addresses the challenge of maintaining stable and adaptable chunk groupings in temporal sequences.

items.title: Brain-Inspired Hierarchical Modularity for General Continual Learning
items.summary: The research proposes a brain-inspired hierarchical modularity principle to address general continual learning under online and uncertain data streams. This approach coordinates experience separation through expert specialization and integration through ensemble methods, drawing inspiration from the Drosophila learning system. The method is implemented by applying lightweight modular adaptation to pre-trained foundation models using random expansion for expert routing and diversified integration across scales. Experimental results show consistent performance improvements across various domains, including vision-language tasks and embodied learning. These findings suggest hierarchical modularity provides a biologically grounded framework for learning from dynamic experience.

items.title: Dual-GNN Multilevel Coarsening for Maximum Independent Set
items.summary: The paper proposes Dual-GNN Multilevel Coarsening to solve the Maximum Independent Set problem efficiently. It introduces Graph Edge Sparsification (GES), a learning-based method for Euclidean TSP that uses geometric and combinatorial information. This approach adaptively generates a sparsification graph to reduce graph size and speed up solving. Experiments show GES can prune up to 95% of edges on the MATILDA dataset while maintaining a solution gap under 1%. The method also demonstrates strong generalization on TSPLIB instances, achieving pruning rates over 99%.

items.title: Exposing Blind Spots in Deep Imbalanced Regression Evaluation
items.summary: Deep Imbalanced Regression (DIR) evaluation has blind spots due to reliance on image benchmarks, non-decision-complete protocols, and unexamined tail-region stability. The authors address these issues by evaluating DIR on multimodal time-series data and introducing balanced metrics like bMAE and bMASE. Re-evaluation across random seeds revealed that DIR methods hide tail degradation in standard evaluations and exhibit uneven transfer to multimodal data. Tail-region instability remains a hidden failure mode in current DIR evaluation practices. These findings provide a reproducible basis for future research in regression systems.

items.title: Learning Neural Feedback Linearization for Data-driven Systems via Augmented Lagrangian
items.summary: A novel data-driven framework is proposed for designing and training a feedback linearizing controller by incorporating relative degree conditions. This method replaces conventional feedback controller components with neural Lie derivatives, creating a fully data-driven framework. The work also establishes sufficient conditions for closed-loop stability when identification errors are bounded. Theoretical results are validated using an armature-controlled DC motor as an application example.

items.title: Mitigating Sequential Reappearance in Diffusion Data-Point Unlearning
items.summary: Diffusion data-point unlearning evaluation often ignores sequential reappearance, where forgotten data reappears later without retraining. The research introduces a target-level evaluation protocol to track whether data is forgotten immediately, remains forgotten, or reappears during subsequent deletions. Targets that reappear later exhibit a sharper local denoising-loss geometry after deletion compared to those that remain forgotten. This behavior suggests a specific pattern in how unlearned data persists in diffusion models. The findings aim to address the failure mode of sequential reappearance in diffusion data-point unlearning.

items.title: What Does Chain-of-Thought Entropy Measure? A Channel Audit of Scaffolding, Routing, and Content
items.summary: Entropy over chain-of-thought tokens determines which tokens receive policy gradient updates, pruning, or collapse decisions. These statistics reflect a mix of emitting scaffolding, choosing the connective structure, and selecting the substantive continuation. Separating these elements allows for distinct measures: entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence, and first-order entropy velocity. The research investigates how raw and content conventions differ regarding the interpretation of these measures across scaffolding, routing, and content channels. Findings suggest that content convention outperforms raw surprisal in compression tasks, and restated answers significantly contribute to chain accuracy.

items.title: FREESIA: Covariance-Aware Posterior Transport for Expressive and Scalable Data Assimilation
items.summary: FREESIA proposes a training-free, asymptotically exact posterior transport method for data assimilation. It introduces a covariance-aware transport scheme to embed forecast cross-covariance and preserve the non-Gaussian posterior structure. The method combines an observation-adaptive proposal with posterior correction for accurate nonlinear posterior approximation. A posterior flow theory is also established to derive the method's asymptotic exactness and Wasserstein error bounds. Experiments on various flows demonstrate the method's accuracy and effectiveness, reducing RMSE by 56% in sparse settings.

items.title: Variational objectives for amortized Bayesian inference in inverse problems: The role of posterior conditioning
items.summary: Variational autoencoders (VAEs) are used for amortized Bayesian inference in inverse problems, but posterior accuracy is sensitive to the chosen variational regularization. The study compares three objectives: VAE-KL, VAE-JS, and VAE-JSWA, which incorporates the 2-Wasserstein distance. Evaluation on benchmarks and nonlinear problems shows that VAE-JSWA yields lower posterior errors in ill-conditioned scenarios. This research suggests that posterior conditioning is a critical factor in selecting variational objectives for Bayesian inverse problems.

items.title: Empirical Auditing of Edge-Private Graph Generators
items.summary: The research empirically audits privacy leakage in edge-private graph generators. It tests whether outputs from edge-neighbouring inputs remain distinguishable using statistically valid lower bounds on privacy loss. The framework compares direct-edge, local-structural, and Graph Neural Network-based attacks around a target edge. Experiments demonstrate that privacy leakage depends on both the mechanism and the network, with learned representations revealing information beyond conventional local statistics.

items.title: Penalized Nonreversible Langevin for Constrained Sampling
items.summary: Penalized nonreversible Langevin algorithms are proposed for sampling from distributions restricted to a compact convex set $\mathcal{C}$. These algorithms use a squared distance penalty along with state-dependent perturbations to preserve a penalized Gibbs distribution. Nonasymptotic total variation bounds and $2$-Wasserstein bounds are established under certain conditions for the full gradient algorithm. Tuning the skew perturbation allows for nonreversible acceleration, improving bounds on the Euler iteration by tuning the imbalance. Numerical experiments validate these methods in constrained Bayesian tasks and stochastic quadratic models.

items.title: PICPIs: Prediction-Interval-Conditional Prediction Intervals
items.summary: Prediction-Interval-Conditional Prediction Intervals (PICPIs) introduce a prediction-based conditioning framework to address limitations in conformal prediction uncertainty quantification. A PICPI is an interval that satisfies a self-consistency condition, ensuring the conditional mean outcome falls within the interval. These intervals create data-adaptive strata without changing the original prediction. Under regularity, these intervals cover most prediction values and have widths that decrease at a rate of $n^{-1/3}$. The work derives inference procedures for PICPIs in prediction and classification tasks with empirical comparisons.

items.title: Scalable Minimum-Volume Simplex Estimation with Non-asymptotic Analysis
items.summary: The research addresses estimating a $K$-dimensional simplex from $N$ uniform samples, noting that existing estimators are computationally prohibitive for large $N$. The authors propose DeepMVSA, a method using a neural implicit form to generate mixing weights and a triangular parameterization for the dual simplex matrix. This approach reduces trainable memory to $O(K^2)$ and achieves a cost per data pass of $O(NK^2)$. Non-asymptotic analysis provides sample-complexity bounds, showing $N^{-1/2}$ scaling is lower-bounded, and experiments validate the performance up to $N=10^8$.

items.title: Generalized Deep Regression for Repeated Measurements
items.summary: The research studies estimating a marginal regression function from independent units with repeated binary, count, or continuous responses using ReLU deep neural networks. The model assumes dependence is generated by an unobserved random mean function within each unit, fitted with a convex generalized regression loss. The work establishes oracle inequalities by separating conditional and between-unit variation, and derives an integrated mean squared error rate for ReLU networks. The paper also provides results for weighted oracle inequalities and pointwise ensemble inference. Simulations and real data support the theoretical findings regarding these regression estimates.

items.title: On the Gradient Heterogeneity Dynamics of Adversarially Robust Federated Regression
items.summary: Federated learning is inherently heterogeneous, further complicated by adversarial clients sharing updates. The paper derives gradient heterogeneity directly from the statistical models of linear and nonlinear regression using fresh data at each round. Bounds are established that separate heterogeneity among honest clients' parameters, label noise, and initialization. Convergence is shown for $(f,\kappa)$-robust aggregators when the adversarial fraction $f/n$ is less than $1/2$. This convergence requires an explicit sample burn-in under specific conditions.
